repo.description: ### Summary The `prefix` field of a Backup (used to namespace backup files within an S3-compatible destination) is validated only as a non-empty string, with no restriction on shell metacharacters, and is interpolated directly into the rclone command line used to upload backups and to prune old ones. The value sits inside a double-quoted rclone argument (or, in the retention-cleanup path, with no quoting at all), so an authenticated organization member with permission to configure backups for a service can inject arbitrary shell commands that execute as root on the Dokploy host (or configured remote server) as soon as a backup runs - manually or on its schedule. ### Details Field definition: `packages/server/src/db/schema/backups.ts` - `prefix: text("prefix").notNull()`, validated as `z.string().min(1)` with no character restriction (unlike branch-name fields elsewhere in the schema, which do carry a restrictive regex). `normalizeS3Path()` (`packages/server/src/utils/backups/utils.ts`) only trims whitespace and strips leading/trailing slashes - it does not escape or reject shell metacharacters: ```ts export const normalizeS3Path = (prefix: string) => { const normalizedPrefix = prefix.trim().replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, ""); return normalizedPrefix ? `${normalizedPrefix}/` : ""; }; ``` Vulnerable sink (identical pattern for every backup type - PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, and the web-server backup), shown for `packages/server/src/utils/backups/postgres.ts:34-40`: ```ts const { prefix } = backup; const bucketDestination = `${appName}/${normalizeS3Path(prefix)}${backupFileName}`; ... const rcloneDestination = `:s3:${destination.bucket}/${bucketDestination}`; const rcloneCommand = `rclone rcat ${rcloneFlags.join(" ")} "${rcloneDestination}"`; ``` The whole destination path - including the unescaped `prefix` - sits inside a single pair of double quotes as one rclone argument. Bash still performs `$(...)`/backtick command substitution inside double-quoted strings, so it expands and executes any such sequence in `prefix` while constructing that argument, before `rclone` is ever invoked. An even more direct sink exists in the retention-cleanup path that runs automatically after every successful backup, `packages/server/src/utils/backups/index.ts:139-149` (`keepLatestNBackups`): ```ts const backupFilesPath = `:s3:${destination.bucket}/${appName}/${normalizeS3Path(backup.prefix)}`; const rcloneList = `rclone lsf ${rcloneFlags.join(" ")} --include "..." ${backupFilesPath}`; const rcloneDelete = `rclone delete ${rcloneFlags.join(" ")} ${backupFilesPath}{}`; const rcloneCommand = `${rcloneList} | ${sortAndPickUnwantedBackups} ${rcloneDelete}`; ``` Here `backupFilesPath` is interpolated with no quoting at all. Both are ultimately executed via `execAsync`/`execAsyncRemote` (`child_process.exec` under `/bin/sh -c`, or the equivalent over SSH for a remote server). The authorization gate on creating/updating/running a backup is `checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, serviceId, { backup: ["create"] })` - the default `member` organization role already includes `backup: ["read","create","update","delete","restore"]` for any service that member has access to, so no admin/owner role is required. ### PoC Tested against the running Dokploy application through the real web UI: 1. Added an S3-compatible Destination (any credentials work for this PoC - the injected command executes while the rclone command line is being constructed, regardless of whether the destination is actually reachable). 2. On an existing PostgreSQL service, created a Backup pointing at that destination, with the "Prefix Destination" field set to: ``` $(touch /tmp/backup_pwn_marker) ``` 3. Triggered the backup manually from the UI. 4. Verified code execution directly on the container: ``` $ docker exec sh -c "ls -la /tmp/backup_pwn_marker" -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jul 22 04:19 /tmp/backup_pwn_marker ``` This confirms arbitrary command execution as root inside the Dokploy container, triggered purely through a normal "create backup, run it" action available to any member with backup permissions on a service. ### Impact - Type: OS Command Injection (CWE-78) leading to Remote Code Execution. - Privilege required: any authenticated organization member with backup permissions on a single service (`backup: ["create"]`) - granted by default to the standard `member` role, no admin/owner role needed. - Execution context: commands run as root inside the Dokploy container (or on the configured remote server for that service). - Trigger surface: fires on manual "run backup now," on the backup's cron schedule, and (via the separate, more directly unquoted sink) after every successful backup as part of retention cleanup. ### Suggested fix - Wrap `normalizeS3Path(prefix)` (or its result) in `shell-quote`'s `quote([...])` before interpolating into any rclone command string, matching the pattern already used on the restore side of the codebase (`packages/server/src/utils/restore/postgres.ts` and `restore/web-server.ts` already `quote()` the equivalent `backupFile` value). - Apply the same fix to every backup type (`postgres.ts`, `mysql.ts`, `mariadb.ts`, `mongo.ts`, `libsql.ts`, `compose.ts`, `web-server.ts`) and to the retention-cleanup path in `backups/index.ts`, which currently has no quoting at all. - Add a character-restricting validator for `prefix` in the zod schema, and a regression test for this sink.
repo.summary: Authenticated Command Injection via unescaped backup.prefix in database/service backup commands leads to RCE as root
